name: Stratholme Service Entrance
summary: At Eastwall Gate in the northern Eastern Plaguelands, the Scourge holds Stratholme's eastern quarter. The Service Entrance cuts through the city's fortified wall.

sections.title: A Breached Bastion
sections.body: Stratholme's Main Gate opens into King's Square, with a road toward the Scarlet Bastion. At Eastwall Gate, the Service Entrance breaks through the eastern fortification. Beyond it lie Elders' Square and blighted paths to Baron Rivendare's slaughterhouses.

sections.title: The Scourge Redoubt
sections.body: The Service Entrance gives a shorter way into Stratholme's eastern districts. The Scourge holds the alleys and ziggurats, guarded by gargoyles, crypt fiends, and cultists. The Argent Dawn and bold adventurers gather here before striking at the Lich King's commanders.

faq.q: Where is the Stratholme Service Entrance located?
aliases: how to find strat back door
faq.answer: The entrance lies at Eastwall Gate, along the northern mountains of the Eastern Plaguelands, just east of Stratholme's main ruins. A stone archway cuts into the fortified wall there.

faq.q: How does this entrance differ from the Stratholme Main Gate?
faq.answer: The Main Gate opens into King's Square and leads across the city toward the Scarlet Bastion. The Service Entrance opens near Elders' Square, closer to the undead-held eastern districts and Slaughter Square.

faq.q: Why is it called the Service Entrance?
faq.answer: The reason for the name Service Entrance is not given.

faq.q: Who controls this part of the city?
faq.answer: The Scourge controls the district beyond the gate. Baron Rivendare and his acolytes oversee it and maintain the ziggurats that anchor their dark magic within Elders' Square.

angles.text: As a paladin, you enter the Scourge's defiled necromantic apparatus. The gate gives you a direct path to purge Rivendare and reclaim the holy city's fallen honor.
As a rogue, you can use the service gate to slip around fortified battle lines and enter the city's utility corridors.
